# Rule 3 - Keep IC and OOC Separate
Keep in-character (IC) interactions in-character, and out-of-character (OOC) interactions out of character.
## Precedents
- LOOC (local out-of-character) chat should be used sparingly and infrequently. You should make a reasonable effort to use IC chats as much as possible to maintain a level of immersion both for yourself and other players. - Do not use the OOC nor LOOC chat to communicate in-character, such as using it to bypass speech restrictions. - Using LOOC to teach someone something that can't be taught in-character, such as the controls of the game, is fine. - Do not say LOOC or OOC things in-character, such as "I just joined the round"; either say it in LOOC or say something like, "I just showed up to this shift." - Lengthy discussions in LOOC about things occurring outside the bounds of the round’s story should not take up the majority of your time spent in round.
